alice: quick sync — ran a focused harness for embedding->rerank endpoint comparing two traffic patterns (synthetic constant-QPS vs replayed production bursts). focusing on kernel selection impact, batching heuristics, and KV cache behavior. TL;DR: p99 tail is dominated by cache misses + large-payload scatter, not matmul kernel switch like we thought :thinking_face:
ben: nice. can you share the exact runs and config? especially batch cutoffs and vector dims.
alice: yup. commands used:
```bash
# replay harness (subset of prod traces, 10M requests total)
python tools/replay_harness.py \  --trace=gs://prod-traces/rerank/2026-02-28-subset.json \  --concurrency=200 \  --max-qps=800 \  --pin-model=rdw/sim-embed-v2 \  --batch-policy=auto

# synthetic steady load
python tools/synth_load.py --pattern=steady --qps=500 --corr=0.02 --payload-scale=1.0
```
carol: what batch-policy variants did you try? auto vs size-based vs latency-based?
alice: tried `auto` (runtime decides kernel+batch), `fixed-N` (N in {1,4,8,16,32}), and `deadline` (max latency 120ms). Also toggled per-request KV cache hints (client-provided prefixes) vs opaque keys.
dmitri: any change in kernel selection logs? i.e. fallback to int8 matmul vs fp16?
alice: yes — runtime knob `kernel_preference=latency|throughput|balanced` moved selection, but most p99 regressions correlate with cache miss amplification, not kernel. sample from profiler (aggregated):
```
PROFILE SNIPPET: rerank/2026-03-07 14:12
- total tokens (avg) per req: 48
- avg batch size (auto): 11.3
- KV cache hit rate: 78% (replay) vs 94% (synth)
- p50/p95/p99 latency (ms): 18 / 46 / 210 (replay)
- tail stack (hotspots): io_kv_lookup 35%, attention_kernels 25%, matmul_16x16 12%, copy/serialize 10%, other 18%
- top kernel variants seen: matmul_fp16_opt, matmul_int8_q8, attention_fp16_block
```
ben: 210ms p99 is rough. is that with payloads including full user metadata? how big were vectors/payloads?
alice: payload scale was 1.0 for replay (real prod size distribution). median vector dims=1536, avg payload size=1.8 KB per request (includes ranking context). synth run used trimmed payloads (0.9KB) which is why synth tail looks fine.
eve: did you try increasing KV cache capacity or sticky routing to reduce miss amplification?
alice: yes — two knobs: more mempool per-shard (KV capacity + sticky routing to keep keys on same worker) reduced miss-rate to 88% and p99 to 120ms in the tuned run. but cost goes up ~22%.
dmitri: any insight on batching heuristics? e.g. bounding batch by sum(payload_size) rather than item count?
alice: great point — we prototyped `batch_by_weight` where each request has a weight ~= payload_size/1KB. results: with `batch_by_weight` we kept effective compute utilization but avoided outlier IO serialization. p99 dropped further to ~95ms with same throughput.
carol: are these apples-to-apples? how did you ensure matching warm starts and model caches? replay vs synth could differ in KV prewarm.
alice: we forced cold-starts between runs and ran a 20 minute preheat phase identical across configs. also pinned model version and prefilled model weights cache. KV prefill was controlled: either zero-prefill or prefill-to-90% for the test matrix. logs annotated with run_id and prefill tag.
perf-bot: LOADTEST/1769954321: run=rdw-rerank-load-20260307-01 status=COMPLETE throughput=760r/s mean_lat=32ms p95=48ms p99=210ms errors=0 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
ben: did you capture syscall traces or per-thread block times? want to know if IO scheduling is the culprit.
alice: we captured eBPF summaries on a subset: main blocker is `recvmsg` + `writev` churn when payload>1.2KB per request. also saw thread context switches spike when KV misses triggered remote fetches.
dmitri: so next actions?
alice: proposal:
- short term: enable `batch_by_weight` in runtime by default for rerank endpoints (opt-in via config flag)
- medium: add sticky routing + adaptive shard sizing for KV to keep miss amplification <10% for common tenant patterns
- long: investigate zero-copy serialize path to reduce copy/serialize 10% overhead and bench again
I can open PRs for the runtime and a follow-up perf ticket for infra KV changes.
carol: +1 to batch_by_weight. please include microbench numbers for small dims (512) and large (2048) vectors so we can show cost tradeoffs.
alice: will do. I'll attach the full run matrix and flamegraphs to the ticket. thanks all. :thumbsup:
